A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMR framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original drift-adaptation experiments, accuracy and forgetting results, computational comparisons, and transformation-severity experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original CLEAR-10 experiments and evaluations with ResNet-152 and ViT-S in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds feature-space MMD detection for CLEAR-10 after finding the original uncertainty-based KS detector insufficiently sensitive. The central flush-and-resample AMR procedure remains unchanged. Algorithm 1 expands the replacement operation already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds CLEAR-10 evaluation using natural temporal changes between early and late image buckets, extending coverage beyond the retained synthetic transformations of four vision benchmarks. This substantially broadens the represented drift conditions.

E2.justification: Corresponding original experiments retain ER, ER-ACE, DER++, SER, and CLS-ER, with the same Vanilla and Full Relearning comparisons. The new CLEAR-10 and backbone studies reuse subsets of these methods; no comparator is removed from a retained experiment or newly introduced.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings remain intact. Appendix B adds a CLEAR-10 protocol excluding BACKGROUND, combining buckets 1–2, shifting recurring classes to buckets 9–10, and using five two-class tasks with a 1000-sample buffer. Appendix C adds ResNet-152 and ViT-S evaluations with ER and a 5000-sample buffer.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds dedicated tests of whether AMR generalizes across deeper convolutional and transformer architectures. Appendix B adds detector-failure and sensitivity analysis, including limited benefits from relaxing the KS threshold and improved detection with MMD. Existing buffer-size, transformation-severity, feature-space, and efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-run averages and unidentified ± quantities; v2 explicitly labels these quantities as standard deviations. Shared results retain the same reporting values and run count. CLEAR-10 also reports three-run averages, while the new backbone table provides point estimates without uncertainty or a stated run count.

E6.justification: All 280 matched main-table entries are unchanged between v1 Tables I–II and v2 Tables 1–4. New Tables 5–6 add substantial results under additional conditions: CLEAR-10 ER achieves 51.50% FAA with AMR versus 47.53% with FR, whereas ER-ACE achieves 53.00% versus 59.33%. Backbone experiments also add new results, rather than same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, four theorems, and their proofs are retained. The new MMD discussion is descriptive and introduces no new formal derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: representation-level drift evaluation, targeted memory realignment, and FR-like performance with lower resource requirements. The revised conclusion incorporates CLEAR-10 evidence without materially redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v1 offers brief future-work remarks about detection. v2 Section 6 substantially develops detector dependence, false alarms, contaminated buffer references, gradual or mixture drift, adversarial concealment, and loss of relevant submodes during replacement. Appendix B additionally interprets weaker natural-drift benefits and ER-ACE’s poorer comparison with FR.

D1.justification: The anonymous implementation link is replaced by a named GitHub repository, now explicitly advertised as providing code and benchmark datasets. CLEAR-10 construction details are added. The original hyperparameter settings are retained and moved from Appendix B to Appendix D; repository contents were not externally verified.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially through discussions of adaptive plasticity, recent drift-detection methods, and the distinction from test-time adaptation. Added examples include PromptFusion, SD-LoRA, BECAME, MCD-DD, and DriftLens, alongside citations supporting CLEAR and MMD.

P1.justification: Most existing introduction, method, theory, and experimental prose remains closely matched. Local revisions expand Algorithm 1, rewrite the conclusion and future-work discussion, and add related-work subheadings. References move before the appendices, while the original hyperparameter appendix becomes Appendix D.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column IEEE layout to a single-column TMLR layout, with substantially enlarged and rearranged figure panels. The two combined results tables become four dataset-specific tables, and hyperparameter displays are consolidated. Figures 15–16 and Tables 5–6 are added; original figure contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1’s synthetic-drift, ResNet-18-only validation through natural temporal data and additional architectures. More decisively, it exposes the original detector’s failures and documents mixed CLEAR-10 outcomes alongside detailed applicability limits, making practical claims more assessable. CLEAR-10 shifts are mild, and backbone results lack uncertainty reporting, but the added validation and explicit failure analysis materially improve the paper’s evidential grounding and transparency.
